choice: Represent the chemistry as parallel methanol synthesis (CO2+3H2→CH3OH+H2O) and reverse water-gas shift (CO2+H2→CO+H2O), using each record's measured methanol selectivity to partition converted CO2; do not extrapolate catalyst-family-specific elementary steps.
alternatives: Single methanol reaction with 100% selectivity
Detailed Langmuir-Hinshelwood mechanism for every catalyst family
CO-mediated sequential mechanism with explicit methanol-from-CO reaction
reason: The dataset spans Cu/Zn, ZnZrOx, In2O3, Pd/In, Pd/Zn and Pt systems with different proposed active sites, while all records consistently provide net CO2 conversion and methanol selectivity. A two-net-reaction representation preserves measured carbon partition and water formation without imposing one family's elementary mechanism on others.
evidence: DOI:10.1016/j.chempr.2019.10.023 (water affects methanol/RWGS selectivity on Cu-ZnO-ZrO2)
DOI:10.1126/sciadv.1701290 (ZnO-ZrO2 selective CO2 hydrogenation performance)
DOI:10.1021/acscatal.9b03305 (In2O3/ZrO2 catalyst-family mechanistic differences)

choice: Transfer measured methanol productivity as the catalyst-specific activity anchor and scale required catalyst inventory by a reversible approach-to-equilibrium driving-force correction at the record T, P and plant composition; enforce equilibrium as a hard conversion ceiling and apply a replacement penalty from reported 10%-activity-loss cycle time when available.
alternatives: Rank and size solely by reported CO2 conversion
Use one universal published Cu/ZnO kinetic law for all catalyst families
Assume laboratory productivity transfers unchanged at any recycle composition
Fit family-specific kinetic parameters from sparse points
reason: Reported conversion is reactor/contact-time dependent, whereas normalized productivity carries activity information. A universal Cu kinetic law would erase observed catalyst differences and be invalid for oxide/intermetallic families; sparse heterogeneous data cannot identify adsorption constants. The reversible driving-force factor captures attenuation near equilibrium and recycle-product inhibition while retaining the measured activity anchor.
evidence: DOI:10.1016/j.cej.2021.129120 (experimental kinetic modeling for In2O3)
DOI:10.3390/catal13101349 (reversible kinetic model for CO2-to-methanol)
DOI:10.1038/s41467-023-36407-1 (activity enhancement and H-supply effects on ZnZrOx)
DOI:10.1126/sciadv.1701290 (reported long-term stability and productivity for ZnO-ZrO2)

choice: Use a pressurized multi-bed fixed-bed catalytic reactor with interbed cooling/heat removal, optimizing per-pass CO2 conversion subject to equilibrium and catalyst activity while retaining each literature record's temperature and pressure as its feasible operating condition.
alternatives: Single adiabatic fixed bed
Slurry reactor
Fluidized bed
Isothermal membrane reactor
Condensing reactor
reason: The screened evidence is overwhelmingly continuous fixed-bed operation on solid catalysts; industrial methanol synthesis requires exotherm control, and interbed cooling permits the model to represent reaction heat removal without assuming unproven slurry, membrane, or in-reactor condensation behavior for all catalyst families.
evidence: DOI:10.1007/s10562-016-1960-x (continuous fixed-bed CO2 methanol testing)
DOI:10.3390/catal7110332 (direct CO2 hydrogenation process over Cu/ZnO/Al2O3)
DOI:10.1126/sciadv.1701290 (fixed-bed ZnO-ZrO2 testing)

choice: Cool and partially condense reactor effluent, remove crude methanol-water in a knockout drum, distill to product methanol purity, recycle the uncondensed H2/CO2-rich gas with a purge, and export water-rich bottoms.
alternatives: Once-through reaction with no recycle
Pressure-swing adsorption of gases before condensation
Reactive/condensing reactor
Membrane-only methanol purification
reason: Methanol and water are condensable while H2, CO2, and RWGS CO remain primarily gaseous; condensation plus distillation is robust across all catalyst records and gas recycle attenuates low per-pass conversion. A purge prevents CO/inert accumulation.
evidence: DOI:10.3389/fenrg.2019.00081 (CO2-to-methanol process simulation with recycle and purification)
DOI:10.3390/catal7110332 (direct CO2 hydrogenation process configuration)
DOI:10.1016/j.jcou.2020.101407 (thermal integration and separation for CO2 hydrogenation methanol)

choice: Battery limits start with purified gaseous CO2 and H2 at modest delivery pressure and end with specification methanol, a water-rich coproduct/waste stream, and a small purge; electrolysis, CO2 capture, oxygen handling, and downstream methanol distribution are outside the plant.
alternatives: Include renewable electricity generation and electrolysis
Include flue-gas CO2 capture and purification
Start from compressed pipeline feeds
Include methanol storage and distribution logistics
reason: The research question isolates catalyst-driven synthesis-plant choice. Upstream technologies would dominate cost and differ independently of catalyst; feed purchase prices and on-site compression preserve their economic influence without conflating catalyst ranking with capture/electrolyzer design.
evidence: Task reaction and model contract specify CO2 and H2 as feeds and CH3OH as product
DOI:10.1016/j.jcou.2020.101407 (separates synthesis-loop analysis from upstream supply choices)

choice: Use a transparent annualized, unit-by-unit nth-of-a-kind cost model: fresh CO2/H2 feed at fixed table prices; electricity and natural gas from the fixed price table; installed capital scaled by each unit's own flow, power, heat duty or catalyst inventory; capital recovery and fixed O&M from the table; catalyst replacement cost from support/manufacturing plus reported elemental loadings and fixed metal prices.
alternatives: Copy a published plant-level methanol cost
Use one aggregate capex factor independent of catalyst and operating point
Exclude catalyst inventory and replacement
Include upstream CO2 capture and electrolysis capital

choice: Do not infer atomistic active-site densities or DFT descriptors across catalyst families; use reported normalized productivity as the activity measure and reported elemental composition only to estimate catalyst replacement material cost from fixed price-table entries.
alternatives: Predict activity from metal identity alone
Assign a universal turnover frequency per exposed metal atom
Use DFT adsorption energies as cross-family descriptors
Ignore catalyst composition and material cost entirely
reason: The literature records do not consistently report dispersion, active-site count, oxidation state, surface area under reaction, or comparable atomistic descriptors. Inferring these would add unsupported precision, whereas measured productivity already captures the net active-site density and intrinsic rate at the tested condition.
